newsitem.title: UK: British Airways up after airport slot report.
newsitem.headline: British Airways up after airport slot report.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc rose in early trading on Friday after a Financial Times report said the European Commission is expected to recommend legislation to allow airlines to trade takeoff and landing slots more openly.

The FT said the move would be seen as good for BA and its controversial proposed alliance with American Airlines. It would create a means for other carriers -- which have objected to the dominant position at London's Heathrow of the planned BA alliance -- to gain access to the airport and could help defuse opposition to the link-up. BA shares were up 13p at 575 by 0732 GMT.
Today's gain lifted the stock to a new intraday record, surpassing the previous peak of 573p set May 24.
Analysts said the news was also positive for BA since it would crystalise the value of its Heathrow landing slots.
Analyst James Halstead at Credit Lyonnais Laing said BA's balance sheet could be improved by between 2.5 billion stg and 5 billion if the value of its Heathrow position was included.
"It's very much the FT report that has boosted the stock," said one analyst.
Mike Stoddard, analyst at Charterhouse Tilney, said legalising the trade in takeoff and landing slots could be positive for BA's planned alliance with American.
"This would be seen as a positive factor for BA," Stoddard said. "It would help smooth through the American deal it rights became transferrable for cash."
The FT said the EC is expected to recommend changes in slot rules by the end of the year, citing unnamed EC officials who said the Commission is working to regularise existing practice.
The newspaper said slots are at present exchanged at twice-yearly meetings hosted by the International Air Transport Association.
Exchanges are legal providing no money changes hands.
But it also said slots are often traded for a financial consideration.
